Layer-2 applies partialling-out of situational features $\mathbf{X}_2$ to extract pure innovations $\mathbf{Z} = \mathbf{M}_\Phi \mathbf{X}_2$. Finally, Layer-3 performs spectral shrinkage on the residualized kernel $\mathbf{K}_n^\perp$, stabilizing predictions through eigenvalue regularization. This hierarchy prevents overfitting and double-counting while ensuring bounded signal propagation. The Smith Chart transform bounds extreme leverage multipliers, mitigating DFS exposure blowups. Systematic error models are subtracted before variance simulation, aligning with quant-ph/9906014v1. The failure mode of infinite variance arises when $p \ge 2$ adjustments are made on $n_{\text{eff}} = 3$, which is avoided by enforcing $n_{\text{eff}} \ge 8$ or applying shrinkage.
